chapter: Youth, the road and arrival in California
title: Hearing Art Tatum, Hawkins and Eldridge in Cleveland
summary: At the Majestic Hotel scene he first heard Coleman Hawkins, met Roy Eldridge, and sat spellbound at Art Tatum's "Tiger Rag".

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Dancing, singing, you know, comedy. You know, the regular old-time vaudeville that used to come on after the pictures. This is when I was...I was 15 or 16 then. That's when I first met Art Tatum. There was a place called Jimmy Owens, 49th and Central in Cleveland, which was down the street from the Majestic Hotel. The Majestic Hotel is where all the musicians used to stay. That's where I first heard Coleman Hawkins when he was with Fletcher Henderson's band, and that's where I met Roy Eldridge. Roy was 19, and I used to hang out and tag along behind him.

But that's where I first heard Art Tatum. Art Tatum, I remember, was 23 at the time, and I used to go up into this... It was just a joint, you know. And I used to go up there and sit down in a corner by myself, and just listen.

I didn't believe any of what he was doing was possible. There was another piano player, Lannie Scott, and several other guys that I don't remember, but Tatum stuck out in my mind. And he played "Tiger Rag" and all those things... Which incidentally, I have a tape on those things from Tatum from 1935 to '42. This guy Arnold Lovich in New York is a Tatum historian, and he sends me these things.

Anyhow, Tatum was so fantastic, and when he died, what, twenty-two years later I was working with him. He was only 46 when he died. And I had many albums with him during the last years. But this "Tiger Rag", he did it the same way twenty years later as he did then, and it was still fantastic. Nobody could touch him. I had forgotten to mention him. That's when I first heard him.
And Roy Eldridge, too. Roy was a high-note artist then. I think he was working with Fletcher briefly, too. Funny thing, the other night I dreamt about Ben Webster and Coleman Hawkins.
